thread.title: Nasdaq Flattens As Apple Dips; Retailer Breaks Out| Investor's Business Daily

author: ALAN R. ELLIOTT
title: Nasdaq Flattens As Apple Dips; Retailer Breaks Out| Investor's Business Daily
text:
The Nasdaq quickly gave up its opening gains Tuesday, as the Dow dipped to a loss, the dollar held near its 17-month high and oil prices continued to unwind.
X U.K.-based Vodafone ( VOD ) stock was an early leader, surging after it reported its six-month results. Dow stock Home Depot ( HD ) slumped at the open, while Advance Auto Parts ( AAP ) surged on earnings. Marijuana stocks will be in focus on today's stock market , with Cronos Group ( CRON ) down early on its third-quarter results , and group leader Tilray ( TLRY ) set to report after the close.
The Nasdaq Composite and the S&P 500 narrowed to 0.3% gains. The Dow Jones industrial average slipped 0.2% into the red.
Home Depot and Boeing ( BA ) posted the deepest early loses among Dow stocks. Intel ( INTC ) led the Dow, with Nvidia ( NVDA ) and Cree ( CREE ) also scoring strong moves among chipmakers. Vodafone ran atop the Nasdaq 100 and Advance Auto rose furthest among S&P 500 stocks. Apple ( AAPL ) slipped 0.5% as it feels for support at its 200-day line following Monday's 5% sell-off . FANG stock tech leaders turned mixed in early trade, with Facebook ( FB ) leading, up 01%.

The Dow dropped below its 50-day line of support and the S&P 500 cut below support at its 200-day level and flashed a distribution day . The Nasdaq retreated further below its 200-day line, heading for a possible test of its late-October lows, near 7,000. It's a good time for investors to maintain tight sell rules and keep a close eye on the market's status for guidance in making trades.
China Markets Jump; Japan, Oil Slide: Fed Speaks Markets across Asia were sharply mixed. In China, Hong Kong's Hang Seng Index gained 0.6%, and the Shanghai Composite climbed 0.9%. In India, the Bombay Stock Exchange's Sensex jumped 1%.
The confidence didn't carry over into Japan. Tokyo's Nikkei 225 tapped Monday's losses in the U.S. and fell 2.1% — despite the dollar trading near 17-month highs.
European market softened in afternoon trade. Frankfurt's DAX held its 0.7% gain, but the CAC-40 in Paris trimmed its advance to 0.3%, and London's FTSE 100 struggled to hold its break-even line.
Oil prices veered lower, pressured by the rising dollar as well as Monday's comments from President Trump regarding Saudi Arabia's intent to trim its production. West Texas Intermediate stumbled 2.2% to below $59 a barrel. Europe's Brent crude benchmark traded down 2.3% to hold below $69. WTI is now down 24% from an Oct. 3 high.
An otherwise quiet day of economic reports will see speeches from three Federal Reserve officials. Minnesota Reserve Bank President Neel Kashkari speaks in Minneapolis and Fed Governor Lael Brainard delivers comments to a fintech forum in Philadelphia, both at 10 a.m. ET. Philadelphia Federal Reserve Bank President Patrick Harker also addresses the fintech conference, at 2:20 p.m. ET.
Home Depot, Boeing Lag Dow Stocks; Advance Auto Clears Buy Point Boeing dropped 2.7%, the worst early loss among Dow Stocks. News reports Tuesday said the company had failed to alert pilots of possible safety issues related to certain autopilot systems on its new 737 Max jets. The Lion Air jet that crashed and killed 189 persons in Indonesia on Nov. 28 was a 737 Max.
Home Depot dropped 1.4%, despite scoring a big third-quarter beat, maintaining earnings growth of 36%. Revenue rose a slightly better-than expected 5%, while U.S. same-store-sales surged 5.4% . Shares pared back gains to 1.1% in premarket action. The stock is struggling to start up the right side of a two-month consolidation, ending Monday 17% off its September high and below both its 10- and 40-week moving averages.
Pot stock Cronos Group shed 5%, down after reporting a deeper-than-forecast loss of 4 cents per share and a 187% rise in revenue. The volatile stock is deep in a month-long consolidation. Sector peer Tilray dipped 0.8% in premarket trade.
Advance Auto spiked more than 9%, clearing a 171.60 buy point. The retail chain reported a 32% earnings gain and a 4% rise in revenue for its third quarter. Management also raised its full-year revenue and comparable-store-sales guidance to above analyst targets. Advance Auto's gap up open topped a three-weeks tight buy point. The gap-up nature of the move allowed for a 5% buy range beginning at the stock's opening price, 177.51. But be sure to mind the market status indicators when making trades under the current conditions.
Beaten down stocks scored some of Tuesday's strongest premarket moves. Beazer Homes ( BZH ) spiked 15% after its earnings results. Wireless telecom services provider Vodafone popped more than 8% after reporting its first-half performance.
Keurig Dr. Pepper dropped more than 12% ahead of the starting bell. Citigroup maintained its neutral rating on the stock, but lifted its price target to 30, from 26.
Meat producer Tyson Foods ( TSN ) dropped nearly 5% after reporting a mixed fiscal fourth quarter. A 10% earnings gain topped expectations, but revenue slipped 1% — just below analyst targets.
